business_problem: Zalando needed to scale its shopping assistant from a few markets to 25 multilingual markets while improving personalization, instruction following, and recommendation quality without sharply increasing cost.
solution_summary: Zalando rebuilt its shopping assistant around GPT-4o mini and a more granular evaluation framework so personalization could scale across Europe. The first assistant version used GPT-3.5 in a handful of German and English markets, but struggled with nuanced fashion requests, multilingual instruction following, and broad rollout economics. Working with OpenAI, Zalando introduced component-specific evals that score routing and response generation separately and improved few-shot prompts with stronger examples of good and bad recommendations. Once those diagnostics were in place, the team migrated traffic to GPT-4o mini in stages, first moving half the traffic in two weeks and then finishing the rollout across 25 markets. The new stack produces localized recommendations in multiple languages, handles detailed event- and season-specific requests better, and gives Zalando a scalable way to keep improving the assistant as conversational commerce use cases deepen.

data_flow: A shopper request enters the Zalando Assistant, which routes it through the evaluated assistant stack and sends generation tasks to GPT-4o mini. Component-specific evals and few-shot examples monitor routing and recommendation quality so localized responses can be improved before and after rollout across each market.
business_outcome: Zalando increased product clicks by 23%, boosted wishlist additions by more than 40%, scaled the assistant to all 25 markets, and expanded traffic 12x without spending significantly more after moving to GPT-4o mini.
